cues.text: Every AI system today hands you an answer, and a number that claims to know how sure it is.
That number has never been anything more than a guess dressed up as math.
We built the layer that turns it into a guarantee you can check yourself.
Every company racing to put an AI agent into production is about to run into the same wall: regulators.
The EU is now requiring high risk systems to prove their own accuracy, and Gartner has already put a name and a growth curve on this entire category.
This isn't a future problem.
It's happening at the exact moment most systems have nothing to show regulators when they ask.
Nearly half of enterprises using generative AI have already been burned by it in production, and independent testing shows why: accuracy swings wildly depending on who's asking the question.
This isn't hypothetical anymore.
A tribunal held Air Canada responsible for a refund its own chatbot invented, and every one of these failures sounded just as confident as the answer that was actually right.

Conformal Logit Inference sits on top of whatever model you're already running, and turns the confidence it already produces into a real, finite sample guarantee, correct at least as often as you decide it needs to be.
Nothing to retrain, no new model to deploy.
The guarantee was always there.
We just made it provable.
Instead of one flat confidence number, the SDK lets you ask a sharper question, whichever one your decision actually needs.
Underneath, three well established statistical methods share the work, the same techniques researched at MIT, Stanford, Berkeley, and Google.
This isn't a clever heuristic we invented.
It's decades of statistics, finally pointed at large language models.
Here's what that looks like on a real support ticket.
Ask for a Set, and it tells you exactly which queue this belongs in, with a coverage guarantee attached, not just a label.
Then ask for a Gate on whether to auto route it, and this time it escalates instead of guessing, because the bound said this one needed a human.
That's the difference between a score and a guarantee.
This category already has a name, a Gartner report, and a growth curve.
AI Trust, Risk, and Security Management alone is headed toward twenty one billion dollars within a decade, and LLM observability is growing even faster.
Every single company that ships a large language model into production is a future customer of this layer.
This category is already fundable.
Arize, Galileo, and Patronus have all raised real venture money, Guardrails AI was acquired by Harvey, and Weights and Biases sold to CoreWeave for over a billion and a half dollars.
But every one of them tells you what already happened.
None of them gives you a guarantee before it happens, on whatever model you choose to run.
That gap is exactly where we sit, alone.
Pricing is deliberately simple.
Developers can build on it for free, teams pay as usage grows, and enterprise runs entirely inside your own environment when that's what compliance requires.
We're early, and on purpose, we built the hardest part of this business first.
This spreads the way developer tools actually spread.
One engineer installs it in a single line to solve today's problem.
Their team adopts it once it's already running in production.
Compliance signs off last, after the guarantee has already proven itself, not before.
We don't have to sell this in. It sells itself in, from the bottom up.
Every model available today already computes a confidence score.
We're the layer that makes that number mean something you can actually stand behind.
We're raising a pre-seed round to take this from one SDK to the standard every regulated industry checks before it lets an agent ship.
Conformal Logit Inference.
Not a confidence score. A guarantee.
